_note: Sample persona — synthetic. [SIMULATION] 21-day lifelog for the Decision Brain demo: the dream path (home bakery). Maya R. is fictional; every client, neighbor, link and message is invented.

persona.name: Maya R.
persona.headline: AI can’t bake my bread.
persona.dream: Bring back my parents’ bakery, starting from my home kitchen.

fields.career: Eight years as a freelance copywriter for B2B SaaS: blog posts, email sequences, case studies. Clients kept me because I could run a customer interview and explain the product better than their PM. I was good at it. It was never my passion.
fields.now: My biggest client now drafts with AI and only wants light edits: USD 800 a month instead of USD 3,300. I need at least USD 4,000 a month, I have 10 to 12 free hours a week and one child. I cannot lose more money, and I know nothing about running a food business.
fields.pull: My parents ran a bakery for 25 years; it closed in 2019 and I still have my mother’s recipe notebook. “Bakery?” shows up in my notes four times since 2022. What I miss is the Saturday smell and the neighbors who came for bread and stayed to talk.

skills.name: Food safety and cottage food rules

roles.title: AI Draft Editor & Brand Voice Lead

Bake the three best recipes from the notebook and cost each one.

lifelog.title: Dream dump: the bakery
lifelog.summary: Wrote the dream down for the first time: bring back my parents’ bakery, the Saturday smell, the neighbors who came for bread and stayed to talk. Chose the home bakery path. I know nothing about running a food business.

lifelog.title: The push email
lifelog.summary: Biggest client now drafts with AI and only wants light edits: USD 800 a month instead of USD 3,300. Forty percent of my income gone in one email.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 2h 05m
lifelog.summary: Two hours on job boards after the email. Applied to nothing.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 2h 20m
lifelog.summary: Scrolled content jobs until midnight. Every listing says AI-assisted.

lifelog.title: Texas cottage food law explained
lifelog.summary: Explainer: homemade bread can be sold directly to customers from home with a food handler card and labels, no city permit, pickup or in-person delivery only.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 1h 50m
lifelog.summary: More scrolling. Did not open the food handler course.

lifelog.title: Old bakery storefront (2018)
lifelog.summary: Found a photo of the old storefront in the camera roll. Did not post it anywhere.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 2h 00m
lifelog.summary: Two hours again. Closed the laptop feeling behind.

lifelog.title: Message from my brother
lifelog.summary: He sent a photo of mom’s recipe notebook page for the Saturday rolls. “You still have the notebook, right?”

lifelog.title: Opened the course
lifelog.summary: Twenty minutes of the food handler course. Easier than the scrolling.

lifelog.title: Client call: light-edit scope
lifelog.summary: Call with the client that cut the rate. Agreed on light edits for AI drafts, two days a week. The bridge income.

lifelog.title: Test bake: Saturday rolls
lifelog.summary: Baked the first notebook recipe. Ingredient cost USD 2.80 per batch of eight. Wrote it down as the agent asked.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 40m
lifelog.summary: Forty minutes, down from two hours.

lifelog.title: Week 1 review
lifelog.summary: Two of three steps done. Scrolling dropped from two hours to forty minutes. Fear is still there, but so is the bread.

lifelog.title: Walk with my son
lifelog.summary: Sunday walk, no laptop.

lifelog.title: Food handler course: exam passed
lifelog.summary: Passed the online food handler exam. Card arrives this week. Legal to sell from home once the labels are right.

lifelog.title: Label text drafted
lifelog.summary: The agent drafted the cottage food label text; I only had to pick the font.

lifelog.title: Labels printed
lifelog.summary: Printed thirty labels. Food handler card is in the mail.

lifelog.title: How a home bakery found its first 20 customers
lifelog.summary: A home baker’s post: first customers came from a tasting day with neighbors, not from social media.

lifelog.title: Test bake #2: croissant failed twice
lifelog.summary: The notebook croissant collapsed twice. Posted the one good photo on Instagram anyway.

lifelog.title: Light edits: client batch
lifelog.summary: Edited four AI drafts for the bridge client. Two hours.

lifelog.title: Forty likes, three pre-orders
lifelog.summary: The Instagram post got 40 likes and 3 pre-orders. Felt like proof that I am kidding myself. Did not bake.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 1h 10m
lifelog.summary: Back on the job boards for an hour.

lifelog.title: Son home sick
lifelog.summary: Son home with a fever. No baking, no course. Did not want to open the app.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 55m
lifelog.summary: Scrolled while he slept.

lifelog.title: Rested. Reread the notebook
lifelog.summary: Did not bake. Reread the notebook; in the margin of the rolls recipe my mother wrote “bread forgives.”

lifelog.title: Pharmacy pickup reminder
lifelog.summary: Automated text: prescription ready for pickup.

lifelog.title: One loaf, ten minutes
lifelog.summary: Baked one loaf only, ten minutes of hands-on time while the fever broke. The agent said: you did not fail, you took a pause. Test one recipe this week instead of three.

lifelog.title: Week 2 review
lifelog.summary: Three days off. The agent flagged the pattern: a home bakery’s first customers come from tasting, not from likes. Plan: 20 mini loaves for the neighbors.

lifelog.title: Tasting day plan
lifelog.summary: Planned the tasting day with the agent: 20 mini loaves for the neighbors on Sunday, a card and a QR code for pre-orders.

lifelog.title: Free pre-order page template
lifelog.summary: Template for a one-page pre-order site with a QR code and pickup slots.

lifelog.title: Pre-order page is live
lifelog.summary: The agent built the pre-order page. I wrote the bakery story on it: 25 years, the Saturday smell, closed in 2019, back from my kitchen.

lifelog.title: Light edits: client batch
lifelog.summary: Three AI drafts edited. Bridge income on track.

lifelog.title: Coffee with a home baker
lifelog.summary: Coffee with a home baker who sells 30 boxes a weekend from a shared kitchen slot. She started at her own oven, too. First real conversation with someone doing it.

lifelog.title: What she told me
lifelog.summary: Her first customers came from a tasting. Her kitchen slot costs about USD 400 a month for 20 hours; she waited until orders paid for it.

lifelog.title: Saturday box costed
lifelog.summary: Baked and costed the three-recipe Saturday box: one sourdough loaf and four pastries. Ingredients and box about USD 12, price USD 35, margin USD 23.

lifelog.title: Client: edits next week?
lifelog.summary: Bridge client asking whether I can take another light-edit batch next week.

lifelog.title: Shopping list and baking schedule
lifelog.summary: The agent made the shopping list and the baking schedule for Saturday; I approved it in two minutes.

lifelog.title: Job boards: 10m
lifelog.summary: Ten minutes. Closed it.

lifelog.title: Bake day
lifelog.summary: Baked 20 mini loaves for the tasting. Kitchen smelled like Saturday mornings in 2015.

lifelog.title: 20 mini loaves cooling
lifelog.summary: Photo of the loaves on the rack with the cards and QR codes.

lifelog.title: Tasting day with the neighbors
lifelog.summary: Handed out 20 mini loaves on the block. People stayed to talk, like at my parents’ place.

lifelog.title: Eighteen pre-orders. M1: this fits
lifelog.summary: Pre-orders went from 3 to 18 by the evening. Reality check passed: the first Saturday box is on. M1 Fit: yes, this fits me.

lifelog.title: Week 3 review
lifelog.summary: Three of three steps done. Next: first Saturday box, then a shared-kitchen night slot when the oven is full.

day4.note: Two days of job-board scrolling only: app_usage/photo/messenger are not enabled sources, so the brain sees no log since 09-29. Noise is not showing up.

day14.note: micro comeback: one loaf, ten minutes
